question.text: A cylinder is rolling down on an inclined plane of inclination <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math>. Its acceleration during rolling down will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>=</mo></math> _______(use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>).

solution.text:
For rolling motion, the acceleration of the cylinder along the inclined plane can be expressed as

a=gsinθ1+IcmMR2   ...1

The moment of inertia of the cylinder can be written as

Icm=12MR2   ...2

From equations (1) and (2), it follows that

a=gsinθ1+12=2×10×323=103 m s-2

Therefore, x=10.
